chunks: And through this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abi Saeed al-Asfari, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abi al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I and eleven of my descendants, and you, O Ali, are the pegs of the earth; I mean its pegs and its mountains. By us, Allah pegged the earth so that it would not swallow its inhabitants. When the twelfth of my descendants passes away, the earth will swallow its inhabitants and they will not be given respite.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imams being described as the 'pegs of the earth' in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* articulates the cosmological role of the Twelve Imams as 'pegs' (awtad) that stabilize the earth, a concept rooted in Shia eschatology where their absence leads to cosmic upheaval. It explicitly identifies Ali as the first among these pegs alongside the Prophet and the remaining eleven Imams, emphasizing the continuity of divine protection through the specific lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt. The mention of the twelfth Imam’s departure highlights the transition from the era of visible guidance to the Great Occultation, underscoring the enduring spiritual anchor of the Imams even in their absence.
